13.2.14.2

SPI Registers

FCH SPI design is mode 0 only.
This field SpiReadMode[2:0], along with SpiReadMode[0] below, combine to specify the SPI read mode:
Table 161: SpiReadMode[3:0]
Bits
Definition
000b
Normal read (up to 33M)
001b
Reserved
010b
Dual IO (1-1-2)
011b
Quad IO (1-1-4)
100b
Dual IO (1-2-2)
101b
Quad IO (1-4-4)
110b
Normal read (up to 66M)
111b
Fast Read
The SPI configuration registers are accessed through SPI base address specified by FCH::ITF::LPC::BASE_ADDR.
Software can communicate with the SPI ROM through the default memory or an alternate programming method:
• Memory access to the BIOS ROM address space is automatically handled by the hardware. The SPI ROM
controller translates the memory address onto the SPI bus and accesses the SPI ROM data. Any other commands
besides memory read or memory write to the SPI ROM need to go through the alternate programming method.
• With the alternate programming method, software needs to program the SPI_OPCODE, SpiAddress,
TXBYTE_COUNT, RXBYTE_COUNT, put the data into the transmit FIFO, and then execute the command. The
hardware communicates with the SPI ROM using these parameters. This alternate method basically allows
software to issue any flash vendor specific commands such as ERASE and STATUS.
The programming sequence is described as follows.
Change Rom Read mode/Speed:
1. Rom read is handled by old Spi engine first which running 16.7M without prefetch enabled.
[AMD Confidential - Distribution with NDA]

1739

AMD Confidential - Advance Information
56176 Rev 3.10 - Aug 18, 2020

PPR for AMD Family 17h Model 71h B0

2. Program FCH::ITF::SPI::SPI_Cntrl0 to set up Read mode.
3. Program dummy cycle in FCH::ITF::SPI::SPI100_Dummy_Cycle_Config to match the dummy cycle number of
SPI Rom.
4. Program speed for all operations in FCH::ITF::SPI::Spi100Enable.
5. Program UseSpi100 to 1 in FCH::ITF::SPI::Spi100Enable.
6. Porgram PrefetchEnSPIFromHost in FCH::ITF::LPC::LPC_HOSTCONTROL (LPC Cfg 0xBB) to enable read
prefetch.
Command Mode:
1. Set the number of the bytes to be written in FCH::ITF::SPI::TxByteCount[TXBYTE_COUNT] including the
command code in the first byte or the bytes to be read in FCH::ITF::SPI::TxByteCount[RXBYTE_COUNT].
2. Set the command code in SPIx00 FCH::ITF::SPI::SPI_Cntrl0[SPI_OpCode].
3. Put the write data byte into FCH::ITF::SPI::FiFo0~FCH::ITF::SPI::FiFo71.
4. Issue the read status command to SPI device to make sure the SPI device is ready to take commands.
5. Write FCH::ITF::SPI::SPI_Cntrl0[ExecuteOpCode] = 1 to trigger an SPI transaction.
6. Wait for FCH::ITF::SPI::SpiStatus[SpiBusy] == 0 then check bit[7:0] to make sure that the write data and read
data are done correctly.
7. Read FCH::ITF::SPI::FiFo0[FiFoData]~FCH::ITF::SPI::FiFo71[FiFoData] to retrieve the read data.
13.2.14.3

Programming for ROM Protection register

13.2.14.3.1

SPI ROM Physical Address

Using a 64MB SPI ROM as an example, since only address[25:0] are needed for 64MB, SPI ROM will simply ignore
value of address[31:26]. We are using address[31:26]=0x3F, which will make SPI ROM and LPC ROM have same
address. To access SPI ROM, the 64MB SPI ROM are addressed using following physical address:
•
•
•
•

16MB bank-0: 0xFC00_0000 – 0xFCFF_FFFF
16MB bank-1: 0xFD00_0000 – 0xFDFF_FFFF
16MB bank-2: 0xFE00_0000 – 0xFEFF_FFFF
16MB bank-3: 0xFF00_0000 – 0xFFFF_FFFF

13.2.14.3.2

Program ROM Protection Register

Once physical address of protection region is determined, the ROM protection register (LPCx50, LPCx54, LPCx58,
LPCx5C) can be programmed accordingly. Bits[11:0] are straight forward, bits[31:12]: RomBase need to match start
physical address of protection region.
13.2.14.3.2.1

Case-1, 0xFFF0_0000 – 0xFFF0_7FFF

If 32K SPI ROM space at physical address 0xFFF0_0000 – 0xFFF0_7FFF need to have both Write and Read protection,
ROM protection register ((LPCx50, LPCx54, LPCx58, LPCx5C) can be programmed to 0xFFF0_0607.
[7:0]: Range = 0x7, with bit[8] = 0 (unit = 4K), range = 32K
[9] = 1, Read protect
[10] = 1, Write protect
[31:12] = 0xFFF0_0, starting address is 0xFFF0_0000, with range = 32K, the protection region is 0xFFF0_0000 –
0xFFF0_7FFF
13.2.14.3.2.2

Case-2, 0xFD46_0000 – 0xFD4D_FFFF

[AMD Confidential - Distribution with NDA]

1740

AMD Confidential - Advance Information
56176 Rev 3.10 - Aug 18, 2020

PPR for AMD Family 17h Model 71h B0

If 512K SPI ROM space at physical address 0xFD46_0000 – 0xFD4D_FFFF needs to have Write protection only, the
ROM protection register (LPCx50, LPCx54, LPCx58, LPCx5C) can be programmed to 0xFD46_0507.
[7:0]: Range = 0x7, with bit[8] = 1 (unit = 64K), range = 512K
[9] = 0, no Read protect
[10] = 1, Write protect
[31:12] = 0xFD46_0, starting address is 0xFD46_0000, with range = 512K, the protection region is 0xFD46_0000 –
0xFD4D_FFFF
13.2.14.3.3

Index Mode (Indirect) Access

Opcode used in Index Mode determines if it is using 24-bit address mode or 32-bit address mode. For example:
OpCode = 0x03, 24-bit address Read command
= 0x13, 32-bit address Read command
= 0x02, 24-bit address byte program command
= 0x12, 32-bit address byte program command
13.2.14.3.3.1

24-bit Address Index Mode

For Index mode, only address[25:0] are used for ROM protection address comparison. The address mapping of 24-bit
address Index mode is:
Address[31:24]: 0x00, address[25:24] = 00b, point to bank-0 of 64 MB ROM (0xFC00_0000 – 0xFCFF_FFFF)
Address[23:16]: SPI_regx80
Address[15:8]: SPI_regx81
Address[7:0]: SPI_regx82
13.2.14.3.3.2

32-bit Address Index Mode

For Index mode, only address[25:0] are used for ROM protection address comparison. The address mapping of 32-bit
address Index mode is:
Address[31:24]: SPI_regx80, only address[25:24] used.
Address[23:16]: SPI_regx81
Address[15:8]: SPI_regx82
Address[7:0]: SPI_regx83
13.2.14.3.4

Exception

Register ‘ROM Address Override' has been added to change Logical address to Physical address mapping, since
Protection checking is using Address before ‘ROM Address Override' mapping, caution need be paid when ‘ROM
Address Override[4:0]' not equal to 0x0.
Function of ‘ROM Address Override':
1. Bit[3:0] only apply to ROM2 (16MB) space, it is used to change ROM2 logical address to physical address
mapping, it has no effect on ROM1 and ROM3
• Bit[3:0] =0x0 or 0xF, ROM2 (0xFF00_0000 – 0xFFFF_FFFF) map to bank-3 (0xFF00_0000 –
0xFFFF_FFFF)
• Bit[3:0]=0xC, ROM2 (0xFF00_0000 – 0xFFFF_FFFF) map to bank-0 (0xFC00_0000 – 0xFCFF_FFFF)
• Bit[3:0]=0xD, ROM2 (0xFF00_0000 – 0xFFFF_FFFF) map to bank-1 (0xFD00_0000 – 0xFDFF_FFFF)
• Bit[3:0]=0xE, ROM2 (0xFF00_0000 – 0xFFFF_FFFF) map to bank-2 (0xFE00_0000 – 0xFEFF_FFFF)
1. Bit[4] apply to all ROM1/ROM2/ROM3 space. However, since ROM1 and ROM2 are map to 0xFFxx_xxxx by
default, setting bit[4] = 1 will not affect ROM1/ROM2, only ROM3 (64MB) will be map to 0xFFxx_xxxx

[AMD Confidential - Distribution with NDA]

1741

AMD Confidential - Advance Information
56176 Rev 3.10 - Aug 18, 2020

PPR for AMD Family 17h Model 71h B0

(16MB).
• Bit[4]=1, ROM3 (0xfd_0000_0000 – 0xfd_00FF_FFFF) map to bank-3 (0xFF00_0000 – 0xFFFF_FFFF)
• ROM3 (0xfd_0100_0000 – 0xfd_01FF_FFFF) map to bank-3 (0xFF00_0000 – 0xFFFF_FFFF)
• ROM3 (0xfd_0200_0000 – 0xfd_02FF_FFFF) map to bank-3 (0xFF00_0000 – 0xFFFF_FFFF)
• ROM3 (0xfd_0300_0000 – 0xfd_03FF_FFFF) map to bank-3 (0xFF00_0000 – 0xFFFF_FFFF)
13.2.14.3.4.1

Case-1 (0xFFF0_0000 – 0xFFF0_7FFF)

When ‘ROM Address Override' register bit[4:0] != 0x00, there will be following side effects:
• ROM1: no side effect.
• ROM2:
1. Bit[3:0] = 0x0 or 0xF, no side effect.
2. Bit[3:0] = 0xC, host address 0xFFF0_0000 – 0xFFF0_7FFF is blocked.
• Side effect: SPI ROM 0xFCF0 – 0xFCF0_7FFF is protected.
3. Bit[3:0] = 0xD, host address 0xFFF0_0000 – 0xFFF0_7FFF is blocked.
• Side effect: SPI ROM 0xFDF0 – 0xFDF0_7FFF is protected.
4. Bit[3:0] = 0xE, host address 0xFFF0_0000 – 0xFFF0_7FFF is blocked.
• Side effect: SPI ROM 0xFEF0 – 0xFEF0_7FFF is protected.
• ROM3:
1. Bit[4] = 0, no side effect.
2. Bit[4] = 1, since all accesses through ROM3 are maped to 0xFF00_0000 – 0xFFFF_FFFF. If accessed
through 0xFD_0000_0000 – 0xFD_02FF_FFFF, it will access the ROM at 0xFF00_0000 –
0xFFFF_FFFF, which should be protected, but ROM protection comparison will not block it as address
before "ROM Address Override' is used.
• Side effect: Need 3 more protection registers to block "0xFCF0_0000 – 0xFCF0_7FFF" and
"0xFDF0_0000 – 0xFDF0_7FFF" and "0xFEF0_0000 – 0xFEF0_7FFF".
13.2.14.3.4.2

Case-2 (0xFD46_0000 – 0xFD4D_FFFF)

When ‘ROM Address Override' register bit[4:0] != 0x00, there will be following side effects:
• ROM1: no side effect.
• ROM2:
1. Bit[3:0] = 0x0 or 0xF, no side effect.
2. Bit[3:0] = 0xC, no side effect, as ROM2 is mapped to 0xFC00_0000 – 0xFCFF_FFFF.
3. Bit[3:0] = 0xD, since ROM2 is maped to 0xFD00_0000 – 0xFDFF_FFFF, access to ROM2 address
0xFF46_0000 – 0xFF4D_FFFF needs to be blocked, which needs to program another ROM protection
register with 0xFF46_0407.
• Side effect: This will make SPI ROM 0xFF46_0000 – 0xFF4D_FFFF be protected when accessed
through ROM1/ROM3.
4. Bit[3:0] =0xE, no side effect as ROM2 is maped to 0xFE00_0000 – 0xFEFF_FFF.
• ROM3:
1. Bit[4]=0, no side effect
2. Bit[4]=1, for ROM3 (0xfd_0100_0000 – 0xfd_01FF_FFFF) map to bank-3 (0xFF00_0000 –
0xFFFF_FFFF) case, ROM3 range 0xfd_0146_0000 – 0xfd_014D_FFFF will be blocked,
• Side effect: If bit[4]=1, all ROM access (ROM1/ROM2/ROM3) are map to 0xFF00_0000 –
0xFFFF_FFFF, which set protection for 0xFD46_0000 – 0xFD4D_FFFF should not exist.

b) SW programs this byte to be 'nsuccessful completion to instruct the eSPI controller send down unsuccessful
completion

groups to be commnunicated in the same packets.

are defined In current eSPI spec v0.7.
OOB selected: SW programs this byte to be 0x21 to instruct the eSPI controller send send down Tunneled
SMBUS message to slave

The PM register space is accessed through two methods:
• Indirect IO access through IOCD6 [PM_Index] and IOCD7 [PM_Data]. Software first programs the offset into the
index register IOCD6 and then reads from or writes to the data register IOCD7.
• Direct memory mapped access through the AcpiMmio region. The PM registers range from FED8_0000h+300h to
FED8_0000h+3FFh. See PMx04[MmioEn] for details on the AcpiMmio region.

PMx00000004 (FCH::PM::ISACONTROL)
Read-write. Reset: 0000_0002h.
PrtcControl registers are reset by RsmRstB and UsrRstB. RsmRstB is asserted during G3 state. UsrRstB is asserted when
the system reset button is pressed <_in S0 state_>. dPassEnable will be 0 during G3 state so that when S5 power is
down, the invalid values of PrtcControl Registers will be isolated to 0 for PRTC.
One important requirement is:
Rtc32KHz clock's availability should not have any dependency with the PrtcControl Registers. This is because we use
Rtc32KHz clock for various reset de-bounce logics including the reset for PrtcControl Registers.

Bit27 of this register =1

Set bit27=0 will disable timer permanently because bit27 is a sticky bit. Bit27 will reset back to 1 if there is a S5
power loss or it can be written back to 1 by software.
The timer itself cannot be written directly. It will reset back to 0 whenever bit31=1 or bit27=0 or a reset has
occurred.

7:4 poptimersel. Read-write. Reset: 0h.
Description: PopTimer selection:
0000: IDLE-to-OBFF timer. In IDLE state, when PopTimerEn is 1 and the IDLE-to-OBFF event has been lasting
for the time defined in this timer, Wake# is toggled to transist to OBFF state.
0001: OBFF-to-IDLE timer. In OBFF state, when PopTimerEn is 1 and the OBFF-to-IDLE event has been lasting

lasting for the time defined in this timer, Wake# is toggled to transist to ACTIVE state.
0100: OBFF-to-ACTIVE timer. In OBFF state, when PopTimerEn is 1 and the OBFF-to-ACTIVE event has been
lasting for the time defined in this timer, Wake# is toggled to transist to ACTIVE state.
0101: ACTIVE-to-OBFF timer. In ACTIVE state, when PopTimerEn is 1 and the ACTIVE-to-OBFF event has
been lasting for the time defined in this timer, Wake# is toggled to transist to OBFF state.
0110: MinIDLE timer. When PeriodicOBFF is 1 and we are in IDLE state, we will transition to OBFF state once
this timer expires and there is no other conditions requiring us to transition to ACTIVE.
0111: MinOBFF timer. When PeriodicOBFF is 1 and we are in OBFF state, we will transition to IDLE if this
timer expires and there is no other condition that prevents the state from going into IDLE.

13.2.15.5

Power Management (PM2) Registers

The PM2 register space is accessed through two methods:
•
•

Indirect IO access through index/data address pair at IOCD0 [PM2_Index] and IOCD1 [PM2_Data]. Software
first programs the offset into the index register IOCD0 [PM2_Index] and then reads/writes to/from the data
register IOCD1 [PM2_Data].
Memory mapped access through the AcpiMmio region. The ACPI registers range from FED8_0000h+400h to
FED8_0000h+4FFh. See PMx04[MmioEn] for details on the AcpiMmio region.

PM2x00000000 (FCH::PM2::FAN0INPUTCONTROL)

Description: This bit is used to enable the Two Ramp Fan Control Algorithm.
0: Disable
1: Enable
2:0 faninputcontrol. Read-write. Reset: 5h.
Description: 000: FanOut0 is enabled and temperature input is from internal diode.
001: FanOut0 is enabled and temperature input is from Temp0.

011: FanOut0 is enabled and temperature input is from Temp2.
100: FanOut0 is enabled and temperature input is from Temp3.
101: FanOut0 is enabled and temperature input is from TempTsi.

PM2x00000005 (FCH::PM2::MULTIPLIER0)
Read-write. Reset: 00h.
[NOTE] In "Two Ramp Algorithm" mode: The slope value of ramp1hi and ramp0hi is SlopeHi[7:0] = {DutySel[1:0],
Multiplier[5:0]}.
SlopeHi[7:2] are the integer bits and SlopeHi[1:0] are the fractional bits of the ramp slope.
BIOS has to calculate SlopeHi[7:0] using the following equation:
SlopeHi = <_16'hFF00 {Med2Duty0[7:0], 8'b0} _> / <_ HighTemp0[15:0] Hysteresis0[15:0] Med2Temp0[15:0] _>
For example, if our setting is:
Med2Duty0[7:0] = 25% = 40h
HighTemp0[15:0] = 90C = 5A00h
Med2Temp0[15:0] = 40C = 2800h
Hysteresis0[15:0] = 10C = 0A00h
[AMD Confidential - Distribution with NDA]

1842

AMD Confidential - Advance Information
56176 Rev 3.10 - Aug 18, 2020

PPR for AMD Family 17h Model 71h B0

Then:
SlopeHi = <_FF00h 4000h _> / <_ 5A00h 0A00h 2800h _> = 48896 / 10240 = 4.775
Convert the number 4.775 into our 8bit format: 00010011 <_13h_>
BIOS should program Multiplier0 register as 13h in this example.
_aliasHOSTLEGACY; PM2x00000005; PM2=FED8_0400h

PM2x00000010 (FCH::PM2::FAN1INPUTCONTROL)
Read-write. Reset: 00h.
When the fan control is not in AutoMode the active fan duty cycle is set by LowDuty register.
When the fan is set to be controlled by the Temp* input and set to AutoMode, the active duty cycle is controlled by the
hardware automatically either in step or linear function.
<_a_> Step function: If step function is selected, then whenever Temp* reaches the temperature defined by LowTemp
but is less than MedTemp, the fan will be running at a duty cycle equal to LowDuty. When the temperature reaches
MedTemp but is below HighTemp, the fan will be running at MedDuty. When it reaches above HighTemp, the fan will
simply be running 100% duty cycle.
<_b_> Linear function: If linear mode is selected, the duty cycle is determined by the equations below:
When Actual Temperature < LowTemp,
DutyCycle = 0
When Actual Temperature > LowTemp and Actual Temperature < MedTemp
DutyCycle = LowDuty
When Actual Temperature > MedTemp and Actual Temperature < HighTemp
DutyCycle = <_<_Actual Temperature LowTemp_> * <_Multiplier[5:0] + 1_> >> Multiplier[7:6]_> + LowDuty
When Actual Temperature > HighTemp
DutyCycle = max or 100%
In Automode, hysteresis limit <_LinearRange_> is applied to keep the fan from oscillating erratically.
_aliasHOSTLEGACY; PM2x00000010; PM2=FED8_0400h

When the fan control in not in AutoMode, the active fan duty cycle is set by LowDuty register.
When the fan is set to be controlled by the Temp* input and set to AutoMode, the active duty cycle is controlled by the
hardware automatically either in step or linear function.
<_a_> Step function: If step function is selected, then whenever Temp* reaches the temperature defined by LowTemp
but is less than MedTemp, the fan will be running at a duty cycle equal to LowDuty. When the temperature reaches
MedTemp but is below HighTemp, the fan will be running at MedDuty. When it reaches above HighTemp, the fan will
simply be running 100% duty cycle.
<_b_> Linear function: If linear mode is selected, the duty cycle is determined by the equations below:
When Actual Temperature < LowTemp,
DutyCycle = 0
When Actual Temperature > LowTemp and Actual Temperature < MedTemp
DutyCycle = LowDuty
When Actual Temperature > MedTemp and Actual Temperature < HighTemp
DutyCycle = <_<_Actual Temperature LowTemp_> * <_Multiplier[5:0] + 1_> >> Multiplier[7:6]_> + LowDuty
When Actual Temperature > HighTemp
DutyCycle = max or 100%
In Automode, hysteresis limit <_LinearRange_> is applied to keep the fan from oscillating erratically.
_aliasHOSTLEGACY; PM2x00000040; PM2=FED8_0400h

Bits Description
7:3 Reserved.
2:0 faninputcontrol. Read-write. Reset: 0h.
Description: 000: FanOut4 is enabled and temperature input is
from Internal diode.
001: FanOut4 is enabled and temperature input is
from Temp0.
010: FanOut4 is enabled and temperature input is
from Temp1.
011: FanOut4 is enabled and temperature input is
from Temp2.
100: FanOut4 is enabled and temperature input is
from Temp3.
101: FanOut3 is enabled and temperature input is
from TempTsi.
110: FanOut4 is enabled and temperature input is 0.
111: FanOut4 is disabled.

PM2x00000053 (FCH::PM2::MULTIPLIER2_0)
Read-write. Reset: 00h.
[NOTE] In "Two Ramp Algorithm" mode: This register specify the slope value of ramp1lo and ramp0lo.
Multiplier2_0[7:2] are the integer bits and Multiplier2_0[1:0] are the fractional bits of the ramp slope.
BIOS has to calculate Multiplier2_0[7:0] using the following equation:
Multiplier2_0 = <_{Med2Duty0[7:0], 8'b0} {LowDuty0[7:0], 8'b0}_> / <_ Med2Temp0[15:0] MedTemp0[15:0] _>
For example, if our setting is:
Med2Duty0[7:0] = 50% = 80h
LowDuty0[7:0] = 25% = 40h
Med2Temp0[15:0] = 70C = 4600h
MedTemp0[15:0] = 40C = 2800h
Then:
Multiplier2_0 = <_8000h 4000h _> / <_ 4600h 2800h _> = 16384 / 7680 = 2.133
Convert the number 4.775 into our 8bit format: 00001000b <_08h_>
BIOS should program Multiplier0 register as 08h in this example.
_aliasHOSTLEGACY; PM2x00000053; PM2=FED8_0400h

Bits Description
7:0 multiplier2_0_7_0. Read-write. Reset: 00h.
Description: This register is used only when TwoRampAlgorithmEn is 1.
It specifies the slope value of ramp1lo and ramp0lo.
Bit 7~2 are integer bits. Bit 1~0 are fractional bits.

The IOMux register space is accessed through the AcpiMmio region. The registers range from FED8_0000h+D00h to
FED8_0000h+DFFh. See FCH::PM::ISACONTROL[mmioen].
If the platform supports Hardware-reduced ACPI where FCH::PM::ACPICONFIG[acpireducedhwen]==1, then the
GPIO/GEvent pins do not generate SCI (As required per ACPI 5.0 specification). The GPIO pins identified as AGPIO are
capable of generating the interrupt as GPIO-signaled ACPI Events while EGPIO pins function as purely GPIO pins with
no interrupt capability.
AGPIO: Advanced GPIO - this pin can be used for interrupt, wake, or GPIO.
EGPIO: Enhanced GPIO - this pin can be used for GPIO.
If the platform does not support Hardware-reduced ACPI where FCH::PM::ACPICONFIG[acpireducedhwen]==0, then
the GPIO/Gevents function as supported previously.
Override_0/1 columns in the IOMUX Function Table identify pin function in certain circumstances when the IOMUX
selection is ignored. At power-on reset, any ‘*_strap' entry is used to provide advice input for the named function. In SPI
mode, selected when FCH::PM::ACPICONFIG[force_spiusepin_0] ==0, any ‘*SPI*' entry becomes the function of the
pin.
For IOMUX registers, example FCH::IOMUX::IOMUX0_GPIO, there are multi-function IO pin function select
(function-0/function-1/function-2/function-3), it is general description in the table, more detailed description for these
function-0/function-1/function-2/function-3 refer to Table 163 [IOMUX Function Table].

13.2.16.2

GPIO Registers

The GPIO pins are controlled by a combination of device enables and by their specific GPIO and IOMUX register pair.
GPIO registers are accessed through memory-mapped ACPIMMIO region. The offset is relative to FED8_0000h+1500h.
GPIO bank 0 registers range from FED8_0000h+1500h to FED8_0000h+15FFh. GPIO Bank 1 registers range from
FED8_0000h+1600h to FED8_0000h+16FFh. GPIO Bank 2 registers range from FED8_0000h+1700h to
FED8_0000h+17FFh. GPIO Bank 3 registers range from FED8_0000h+1800h to FED8_0000h+18FFh.

GPIOx00000000 (FCH::GPIO::GPIO_0)
Reset: 0004_0000h.
_aliasHOSTLEGACY; GPIOx00000000; GPIO=FED8_1500h

Bits Description
31 less10secsts. Read-write. Reset: 0.
Description: Read-only. This bit is only valid for GPIO0. For other GPIO, this bit is Reserved.
When power button is pressed for less than 10 second in S0 state, this bit will become 1. This bit can be cleared
by writing 1 to InterruptSts bit.
30 less2secsts. Read-write. Reset: 0.
Description: Read-only. This bit is only valid for GPIO0. For other GPIO, this bit is Reserved.
When power button is pressed for less than 2 second in S0 state, this bit will become 1. When Less2secSts
becomes 1, Less10secSts will also become 1. This bit can be cleared by writing 1 to InterruptSts bit.
29 wakests. Read-write,Read,Write-1-to-clear. Reset: 0.
Description: 0: the pin doesn't generate wake event.
1: the pin is one of wake source
Writing 1 to clear the bit to 0.
28 interruptsts. Read-write,Read,Write-1-to-clear. Reset: 0.
Description: 0: the pin doesn't cause interrupt.
1: the pin is one of interrupt source
Writing 1 to clear the bit to 0.
27:26 Reserved.
25 swcntrlen. Read-write. Reset: 0.
Description: 0: Disable software controlled GPIO in
1: Enable software controlled GPIO in
24 swcntrlin. Read-write. Reset: 0. When SwCntrlEn is 1, this bit can be used by software to control the GPIO input
to the GPIO controller. This might be useful during debug or work-around.
23 outputenable. Read-write. Reset: 0.
Description: 0: Output is disabled on the pin
1: Output is enabled on the pin.
22 outputvalue. Read-write. Reset: 0.
Description: 0: low.
1: high.
21 pulldownenable. Read-write. Reset: 0.
Description: 0: Pull-down is disabled on the pin.
1: Pull-down is enabled on the pin.
20 pullupenable. Read-write. Reset: 0.
Description: 0: Pull-up is disabled on the pin.
1: Pull-up is enabled on the pin.
19 Reserved.
18:17 drvstrengthsel. Read-write. Reset: 2h.

14 System Hub (SYSHUB)

14.1

Overview

The System Hub is a crossbar switch used to connect the high speed IO logic into the system. This allows the high speed
IO devices to quickly and efficiently access the memory controllers on the system while allowing efficient priority control
preventing any high speed interface from dominating the memory controller.
This following sections describe the System Hub and IO capabilities.
14.2

SATA

14.2.1

Definitions

Table 174: Link Definitions
Term
Description
HBA
Host Bus Adapter.
PXCMD
Port x Command and Status. X indicates port number. Refer to registers
SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CMD.
14.2.2

SATA Functional Overview

The following sections describe the register programming requirements for proper operation of the integrated SATA for
the processor.
14.2.2.1

SATA Main Features

Supported features:
• Gen I (1.5Gbps), Gen II (3.0Gbps), and Gen III (6.0Gbps) rates are supported
• Spread spectrum clocking is supported on receive sides
• AHCI 1.3.1 compliant
• 64 bit addressing
• NCQ (Native Command Queuing)
• SNotification
• Mechanical presence switch
• Staggered spin-up
• Aggressive link power management
• Command list override
• Command completion coalescing
• Port multiplier
• FIS (Frame Information Structure) based Switching (FBS)
• AHCI mode only
• Supported capabilities are defined in PXCMD register
• Automatic partial to slumber transitions
SATA II supported features:
[AMD Confidential - Distribution with NDA]

Port Multiplier; supports up to 15 devices per port
NCQ (Native Command Queuing) – up to 32 command queues for each device
Auto-Active in DMA Setup FIS
Asynchronous signal recovery
Asynchronous Notification
SATA power management features
• SATA Link Power management - support both partial and slumber modes
• Support both host initiated and device initiated LPM
• Support Asynchronous Notification
• Unused SATA ports can be disabled for lower power state
• Device Sleep

Miscellaneous features:
• SGPIO
• BIST; All legal BIST transmission, reception, and loopback schemes supported for signal integrity analysis
• Hot Plug; 100ms timer to ping external device (except after power-down to PARTIAL/SLUMBER modes)
• Host and device initiated interface power management
• Independent bus master channel for each port allows supporting simultaneous bus master transfers on all ports
• 64-bit addressing
• Fuse Strap

Bits Description
31 GHC_GHC_AE. Read-write. Reset: 1. 0=Disable. 1=Enable. AHCI enable. Setting to 1 indicates that
communication to the HBA is via AHCI mechanisms. This is used by an HBA that supports both legacy
mechanisms (such as SFF-8038i) and AHCI to know when the HBA is running under an AHCI driver. When set,
software shall only communicate with the HBA using AHCI.
30:3 Reserved.
2 GHC_GHC_MRSM. Read-only. Reset: 0. 0=HBA has not reverted to single MSI mode (i.e., Hardware is
already in single MSI mode, software has allocated the number messages requested, or hardware is sharing
interrupt vectors if MC[MME < MC[MMC]). 1=HBA requested more than one MSA vector, but has reverted to
using the first vector only.
Description: MSI Revert to Single Message. Setting to 1 by hardware indicates HBA requested more than one
MSI vector, but has reverted to using the first vector only.
When this bit is cleard to 0, HBA has not reverted to single MSI mode (i.e., hardware is already in single MSI
mode, software has allocated the number of messages requested, or hardware is sharing interrupt vectors if
MC[MME] < MC[MMC]).
HBA may revert to single MSI mode when the number of vectors allocated by the host is less than the number
requested.
This bit shall only be set to 1 when the following conditions hold:
- MC[MSIE] = 1 (MSI is enabled).
- MC[MMC] > 0 (multiple messages requested).
- MC[MME] > 0 (more than one message allocated).
- MC[MME] != MC[MMC] (messages allocated no equal to number requested).
When this bit is set to 1, single MSI mode operation is in use and software is responsible for clearing bits in
SYSHUB::SATA::AHCI::SATA_AHCI_GHC_IS to clear interrupts.

Bits Description
31 P_IS_CPDS. Read,Write-1-to-clear. Reset: 0. 0=No interrupt. 1=Cold Port Detect Status (CPDS) interrupt set.
Cold Port Detect Status (CPDS) interrupt status. When set, a device status has changed as detected by the cold
presence detect logic.
30 P_IS_TFES. Read,Write-1-to-clear. Reset: 0. 0=No interrupt. 1=Task File Error Status (TFES) interrupt set. Task
File Error Status (TFES) interrupt status. This bit is set whenever the status register is updated by the device and
the error bit (bit[0] of the Status field in the received FIS) is set.
29 P_IS_HBFS. Read,Write-1-to-clear. Reset: 0. 0=No interrupt. 1=Host Bus Fatal Error Status (HBFS) interrupt
set. Host Bus Fatal Error Status (HBFS) interrupt status. Indicates that the HBA encountered a host bus error that
it cannot recover from, such as a bad software pointer.
28 P_IS_HBDS. Read,Write-1-to-clear. Reset: 0. 0=No interrupt. 1=Host Bus Data Error Status (HBDS) interrupt
set. Host Bus Data error Status (HBDS) interrupt status. Indicates that the HBA encountered a data error
(uncorrectable ECC / parity) when Reading from or Writing to system memory.
27 P_IS_IFS. Read,Write-1-to-clear. Reset: 0. 0=No interrupt. 1=Interface Fatal Error Status (IFS) interrupt set.
Interface Fatal Error Status (IFS) interrupt status. Indicates that the HBA encountered an error on the Serial ATA
interface, which caused the transfer to stop.
26 P_IS_INFS. Read,Write-1-to-clear. Reset: 0. 0=No interrupt. 1=Interface Non-fatal Error Status (INFS) interrupt
set. Interface Non-fatal Error Status (INFS) interrupt status. Indicates that the HBA encountered an error on the
Serial ATA interface and was able to continue operation.
25 Reserved.
24 P_IS_OFS. Read,Write-1-to-clear. Reset: 0. 0=No interrupt. 1=Overflow Status (OFS) interrupt set. Overflow
Status (OFS) interrupt status. Indicates that the HBA received more bytes from a device than was specified in the
PRD table for the command.
23 P_IS_IPMS. Read,Write-1-to-clear. Reset: 0. 0=No interrupt. 1=Incorrect Port Multiplier Status (IPMS) interrupt
set. Incorrect Port Multiplier Status (IPMS) interrupt status. Indicates that the HBA received an FIS from a device
that did not have a command outstanding. The IPMS bit may be set during enumeration of devices on a Port
Multiplier due to the normal Port Multiplier enumeration process. It is recommended that IPMS only be used after
enumeration is complete on the Port Multiplier. IPMS is not set when an asynchronous notification is received (a
Set Device Bits FIS with the Notification bit[N] == 1, see
SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_NTF[P_NTF_PMN]).
22 P_IS_PRCS. Read-only. Reset: 0. 0=No interrupt. 1=PHY Ready Change Status (PRCS) interrupt set. PHY
Ready Change Status (PRCS) interrupt status. When set to 1, indicates the internal PhyRdy signal changed state.
Reflects the state of SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_SERR[P_SERR_DIAG_N]. To clear this bit,
software Writes (SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_SERR[P_SERR_DIAG_N] = 1) to it clear it to 0.
21:8 Reserved.
7 P_IS_DMPS. Read,Write-1-to-clear. Reset: 0. 0=No interrupt. 1=Device Mechanical Presence Status (DMPS)

interrupt set. Device Mechanical Presence Status (DMPS) interrupt status. When set, indicates that a mechanical

Descriptor Processed interrupt status (DPS). When the bit is set, a PRD with bit[I] == 1 has transferred all of its

into system memory. Cleared by setting SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_SERR[P_SERR_DIAG_F] =
0. NOTE: This bit does not directly reflect SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_SERR[P_SERR_DIAG_F].
SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_SERR[P_SERR_DIAG_F] is set immediately when an unknown FIS
is detected, where this bit is set when the FIS is posted to memory. Software should wait to act on an unknown
FIS until P_IS_UFS == 1, or the two bits may get out of synchronization.

DMA Setup FIS interrupt status (DSS). When the bit is set, a DMA Setup FIS has been received with bit[I] == 1
and has been copied into system memory.
P_IS_PSS. Read,Write-1-to-clear. Reset: 0. 0=No interrupt. 1=PIO Setup FIS Interrupt (PSS) interrupt set. PIO
Setup FIS interrupt status (PSS). When the bit is set, A PIO Setup FIS has been received with bit[I] == 1, and it
has been copied into system memory. The data related to that FIS has been transferred. This bit is set even if the
data transfer resulted in an error.
P_IS_DHRS. Read,Write-1-to-clear. Reset: 0. 0=No interrupt. 1=Device to Host Register FIS Interrupt (DHRS)
interrupt set. Device to Host Register FIS interrupt status (DHRS). When the bit is set, a D2H Register FIS has
been received with bit[I] == 1, and has been copied into system memory.

SATA0AHCIx00000140...SATA1AHCIx000004C0 (SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_FBSS)
Reset: 0000_2000h.
Used to control and obtain status for Port Multiplier FIS-based switching.
_instSATA0_port[7:0]_aliasSMN; SATA0AHCIx0000_0[4C,44,3C,34,2C,24,1C,14]0; SATA0AHCI=0310_1000h
_instSATA1_port[7:0]_aliasSMN; SATA1AHCIx0000_0[4C,44,3C,34,2C,24,1C,14]0; SATA1AHCI=0320_1000h

Bits Description
31:20 Reserved.
19:16 P_FBSS_DWE. Read-only. Reset: 0h. Device With Error (DWE). Set by hardware to the value of the Port
Multiplier port number of the device that experienced a fatal error condition. This field is only valid when
P_FBSS_SDE = 1.
15:12 P_FBSS_ADO. Read-only. Reset: 2h. Active Device Optimization (ADO). Exposes the number of active devices
for which the FIS-based switching implementation has been optimized. The minimum value for this field is 2,
indicating that at least two devices may be active with high performance maintained.
11:8 P_FBSS_DEV. Read-write. Reset: 0h. Device to Issue (DEV). Set by software to the Port Multiplier port value of
the next command to issue.
7:3 Reserved.
2 P_FBSS_SDE. Read-only. Reset: 0. 0=When a falal error condition occurs, the error applies to the entire port and
to clear the error, software sets SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CMD[P_CMD_ST] = 0. 1=When a
fatal error condition occurs, hardware believes the error is localized to one device such that software's first error
recover step should be to utilize the P_FBSS_DEC functionality. Single Device error (SDE). This bit is cleared on
setting P_FBSS_DEC = 1 or upon clearing SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CMD[P_CMD_ST] = 0.
1 P_FBSS_DEC. Read-write. Reset: 0. 0=When hardware has completed the error recover actions, hardware clears
this bit. 1=When stot to 1 by software, the HBA clears the device specific error condition and the HBA flushes
any commands outstanding for the device that experienced the error, including clearing the corresponding
SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_SACT and SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CI bits for that
device to 0. Device error Clear (DEC). A write of 0 by software has no effect. Software only sets this bit to 1 if
(P_FBSS_En && P_FBSS_SDE) == 1.
0 P_FBSS_En. Read-write. Reset: 0. 0=FIS-based switching is not being used. 1=A Port Multiplier is attached and
the HBA uses FIS-based switching to communicate with it. Enable (EN). Software only changes the value of this
bit when SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CMD[P_CMD_ST] == 0.
SATA0AHCIx00000144...SATA1AHCIx000004C4 (SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_DEVSLP)
Reset: 0000_0000h.

multiplier that the HBA applies to the specified DITO value, effectively extending the range of DITO from 1 ms
to 16383 ms. The HBA computes the total idle timeout as a product of P_DEVSLP_DITO and P_DEVSLP_DM
(i.e., DITOactual = P_DEVSLP_DITO * (P_DEVSLP_DM + 1)).

24:15 P_DEVSLP_DITO. Read-write. Reset: 000h.
Description: Device Sleep Idle Timeout (DITO). This field specifies the amount of the time (in approximate 1 ms
granularity) that the HBA shall wait before driving the DEVSLP signal.
Software shall only set this value when (SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CMD[P_CMD_ST] &&
P_DEVSLP_ADSE) == 0. See also P_DEVSLP_DM.
14:10 P_DEVSLP_MDAT. Read-write. Reset: 00h.
Description: Minimum Device Sleep Assertion Time (MDAT). This field specifies the minimum amount of time
(in 1 ms granularity) that the HBA must assert the DEVSLP signal before it is de-asserted. The nominal value is
10 ms and the minimum is 1 ms, depending on device identification information.
Software only sets this value when (SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CMD[P_CMD_ST] &&
P_DEVSLP_ADSE) == 0, and prior to setting SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CMD[P_CMD_ICC] =
8h.
9:2 P_DEVSLP_DETO. Read-write. Reset: 00h.
Description: Device Sleep Exit Timeout (DETO). This field specifies the maximum duration (in approximate 1
ms granularity) from DEVSLP de-assertion until the device is ready to accept OOB. The nominal value is 20 ms
and the maximum value is 255 ms, depending on device identification information.
Software only sets this value when (SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CMD[P_CMD_ST] &&
P_DEVSLP_ADSE) == 0, and prior to setting SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CMD[P_CMD_ICC] =
8h.
1 P_DEVSLP_DSP. Read-only. Reset: 0. 0=The platform does not support Device Sleep on this port. 1=The
platform supports Device Sleep on this port. Device Sleep Present (DSP). Can only be set to 1 if
SYSHUB::SATA::AHCI::SATA_AHCI_HBA_CAP_EXT[GHC_CAP2_SDS] == 1. P_DEVSLP_DSP is
mutually exclusive with (SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CMD[P_CMD_HPCP] &&
SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CMD[P_CMD_ESP]).
0 P_DEVSLP_ADSE. Read-write. Reset: 0. 0=The HBA does not enter DevSleep unless software directed via
SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CMD[P_CMD_ICC].
1=(SYSHUB::SATA::AHCI::SATA_AHCI_HBA_CAP_EXT[GHC_CAP2_DESO]) ? The HBA asserts the
DEVSLP signal after the port has been idle ((SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CI &&
SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_SACT) == 0) for the amount of time specified by P_DEVSLP_DITO
and the interface is in Slumber (SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_SSTS[P_SSTS_IPM] == 6). : The
HBA asserts the DEVSLP signal after the port has been idle ((SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_CI &&
SYSHUB::SATA::PORT::SATA_AHCI_P_SACT) == 0) for the amount of time specified by P_DEVSLP_DITO.
Aggressive Device sleep Enable (ADSE). This bit can only be set to 1 if P_DEVSLP_DSP == 1.

this field will be written to the internal copies of SGPIO registers.
14.3

USB

This section describes the USB3.1 host controller.
14.3.1

USB Functional Overview

This document includes the BIOS and SMU FW change requests for USB.
USB has one USB container:USB0, it contains an xHCI host controller, one four-lane USB31 PHY and Six one-lane
USB20 PHYs.

[AMD Confidential - Distribution with NDA]

2375

AMD Confidential - Advance Information
56176 Rev 3.10 - Aug 18, 2020
14.3.2

PPR for AMD Family 17h Model 71h B0

USB Programming Guide

14.3.2.1

Programming Architecture

The majority of USB register programming sequences are implemented via SMU FW. The primary role of the BIOS is to
signal SMU to execute appropriate Reset or Power State programming sequence.
14.3.2.1.1

BIOS-to-SMU Messages

The following messages are defined for the BIOS to communicate with the SMU:
• USB_COLD_RESET_STAR
• Signal SMU to execute Cold Reset, System Reset, S4/S5 Exit sequence.
• USB_S3_ENTRY
• Signal SMU to execute S3 Entry sequence.
• USB_S3_EXIT
• Signal SMU to execute S3 Exit sequence.
• USB_CONFIG
• Information for platform dependent and independent registers to be programmed by SMU FW in USB
sequences.
• Parameter fields are used for host, group, and various configuration related information. Refer to
14.3.2.1.2 [USB Register Groups] and 14.3.2.1.3 [USB_CONFIG Messages].
14.3.2.1.2

USB Register Groups

USB registers fall into three categories that are differentiated by when they need to be programmed.
• Group 1: USB Container Registers, USB PD I2C Slave Registers, and TCA Registers
• Programmed before reset is de-asserted to PHY and Host Controller.
• Programmed per cold-boot, warm-reset, and S4/S5 exit.
• Group 2: USB PHY Internal Registers
• Programmed after reset is de-asserted to PHY, but before reset is de-asserted to Host Controller.
• Programmed per cold-boot, warm-reset, S4/S5 exit, and link-reset.
• Group 3: USB IP Core Registers
• Programmed after reset is de-asserted to PHY and Host Controller
• Programmed per cold-boot, warm-reset, S4/S5 exit, link-reset, S3 exit, and D3 exit.
14.3.2.1.3

USB_CONFIG Messages

USB_CONFIG messages are defined to pass the programming information of the 3 groups of platform independent and
dependent registers from BIOS and SMU FW.
For the 3 groups of registers, SMU FW needs to store groups 2 and group 3 values as they need to be reprogrammed in
system cycles where BIOS is not available and can't pass the register information to FW. The system cycles include link
resets and USB D3 cycles.
SMU FW shall be implemented in a general way that all USB registers passed through the messages are supported.
14.3.2.1.3.1

USB_CONFIG Message Format

The software messages have 5 DW parameters. USB_CONFIG message uses 4 DW of the parameters. The message
formats are defined in following tables.

14.3.2.2

Reset and Power State Transition Sequences

There are six primary resets and power-state transition sequences:
• Link Reset
• D3 Entry
• D3 Exit
• Cold Reset, System Reset, S4/S5 Exit
• S3/S4/S5 Entry
• Includes Isolation Entry sequence
• S3 Exit
• Includes Isolation Exit sequence
• S0I3 Entry
• S0I3 Exit

14.3.2.2.1.1

Link Reset Re-Initialization

Following the Link Reset Sequence, SMU FW shall re-initialize USB host controller by following the steps under "Cold
Boot, System Reset, S4/S5 Exit, Link Reset Initialization (SMU)".
14.3.2.2.2

D3Hot/D3Cold Entry(SMU)

Following is the SMU FW flow for USB D0 to D3Hot/D3Cold transition. The D3 entry sequence covers all 3 cases,
D3Hot entry, D3Cold-in-S0 entry, and S3/S4/S5 D3 entry.
1. OS/Driver programs USB PMCSR register (in nBIF) to D3.
1. The register writes triggers nBIF interrupt to SMU.
2. On detection of the nBIF interrupt on USB transition from D0 to D3, SMU check the USB_CONFIG message
sent by BIOS to get the USB_PORT0_DISABLE_FLAG. If USB_PORT0_DISABLE_FLAG is 1, program the
register bits below.
1. FCHUSBDWCUSB31CNTR0::PORTSC_20_REGS0_PORTSC_20[WCE] = 1'b0
(0x16C0_0420/0x16E0_0420)
2. FCHUSBDWCUSB31CNTR0::PORTSC_20_REGS0_PORTSC_20[WDE] = 1'b0
(0x16C0_0420/0x16E0_0420)
3. SMU program
USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::SMU_ASSIST_POWER_STATE_CONTROL_CNTR
0[SMU_CTL_POWER_STATE] to 2'b11 (0x16D8_001C[1:0]/0x16F8_001C[1:0])
4. Read
USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::CURRENT_POWER_STATE_CNTR0[CURRENT_POWER_STATE]
and wait until the read value is 2'b11 (D3 state). The step may take up to T_UsbD3Entry.
5. Clear nBIF interrupt.
14.3.2.2.3

D3Hot/D3Cold Exit(SMU)

Following is the SMU FW flow for USB D3Hot/D3Cold to D0 transition. The D3 exit sequence covers D3Hot exit and
D3Cold-in-S0 exit. D3Cold exit during S3 exit is covered in a later section.
1. OS/Driver programs USB PMCSR register (in nBIF) to D0.
a) The register write triggers nBIF interrupt to SMU.
2. On detection of the nBIF interrupt on USB transition from D3 to D0, program
USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::SMU_ASSIST_POWER_STATE_CONTROL_CNTR
0[SMU_CTL_POWER_STATE] to 2'b00
3. Poll USB SMU assist Power State Control register, Current_power_state bits
(USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::CURRENT_POWER_STATE_CNTR
0[CURRENT_POWER_STATE]) until the read value is 2'b00 (D0 state). The step may take T_UsbD3Exit.
a) .
4. Program USB Host Controller(Group 3) registers.
a) Platform-Independent Configuration Programming.
b) Platform-Dependent Configuration Programming.

PPR for AMD Family 17h Model 71h B0

5. Below steps to work around multiple PME_STATUS clear issue.
a) Read from USB Shadowed PMCSR register, PME_Status bit ().
b) If PME_Status bit is 0, write 0 to PME_Status bit () again with other bits unaltered.
c) If PME_Status bit is 1, skip.
6. Clear nBIF interrupt.
14.3.2.2.4

Cold Boot, System Reset, and S4/S5 Exit

After power-up (cold boot), system reset, or S4/S5 exit, BIOS needs to inform FW for the system power state and SMU
FW needs to go through following sequence to initialize or reinitialize the whole USB host.
14.3.2.2.4.1

Cold Boot, System Reset, S4/S5 Exit(BIOS)

1. BIOS sends USB_CONFIG messages with opcode 0x01 to pass programming information of platform
independent and dependent registers to SMU FW.
2. BIOS sends USB_CONFIG messages with opcode 0xC0 to pass sub-sequence enable information.
• Currently there's one sub-sequence, external PHY FW loading to PHY SRAM, for A0.
• The sub-sequence is required for USB0.
• The loading is required per cold boot.
• The sub-sequence is defined in 14.3.2.4.2 [Sub-Sequence].
3. BIOS sends USB_COLD_RESET_START message to SMU FW to perform USB initialization sequence for cold
boot, system reset, or S4/S5 exit.
14.3.2.2.4.2

Cold Boot, System Reset, S4/S5 Exit, Link Reset Init (SMU)

Upon receiving message from BIOS to perform USB initialization sequence for cold boot, system reset or S4/S5 exit,
SMU performs the following programming sequence. This initialization sequence is also performed after a link reset.
The initialization sequence below contains some steps which are redundant (i.e. the register programmed in that step
already has the proper value). However, this allows a common initialization sequence among cold boot, system reset,
S4/S5 exit, and link reset.
1. After SMU FW receives USB_CONFIG messages from BIOS for all register programming information for all
groups (Group1, Group2, and Group3), SMU FW saves all the register programming information.
2. After SMU FW receives USB_COLD_REST_START message from BIOS for boot-up start, SMU FW starts
below steps. Program to 0 to select PERSTb as Sx state exit trigger.
3. Program USB SMU assist Power State Control register, SMU_FW_assist_D_state bits
(USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::SMU_ASSIST_POWER_STATE_CONTROL_CNTR
0[SMU_FW_ASSIST_D_STATE]) to 1 to select USB SMU assist Power State Control register for controller
power management.
4. Program USB SMU assist Power State Control register, SMU_CTL_Power_State bits
USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::SMU_ASSIST_POWER_STATE_CONTROL_CNTR
0[SMU_CTL_POWER_STATE] to 2'b00.
a.The step is redundant for cold-boot and system resets but allows for a common sequence for cold boot,
system reset, and S4/S5 exit.
5. Poll USB Current Power State register, current_power_state bits
(USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::CURRENT_POWER_STATE_CNTR
0[CURRENT_POWER_STATE]) until the read value is 2'b00 (D0 state). Note the step may take T_UsbD3Exit
for S4/S5 exit (where USB host is initially in D3).
6. Program the following USB Container Registers to enable DF_Allow_Pstate_Chg0, override
USB2SINK_PM_Exit_Req to 0, and enable periodic idle interval interrupt.
for periodic idle interval interrupt Enable, please refer to chapter 14.3.2.12 [Periodic idle interval interrupt
Handling].
[AMD Confidential - Distribution with NDA]

USB_SOFT_CONTROLLER_RESET and USB_SOFT_PHY_RESET so they can be de-asserted
individually.
b.In the case of S4/S5 Exit, USB_S5_RESET=0 before this programming step, which sets USB_S5_RESET
to reset the USB Host and PHY.

a.Platform-Independent Configuration Programming
b.Platform-Dependent Configuration Programming

USB0, based on host_number in the message, to 1'b0.
a.The step is required because USB31 PHY firmware from an external source (rather than the built-in version)
needs to be used.
b.The step clears the default USB31 PHY SRAM bypass mode and that is required to load PHY firmware to
PHY SRAM. The step needs to be done before PHY reset is de-asserted.
c.The firmware loading sub-sequence can be executed only after PHY reset is de-asserted.
13. Program USB_S5_RESET = 0.
14. Program USB_SOFT_PHY_RESET = 0.
15. Wait at least T_PhySoftRstOff.
16. Program USB PHY Registers (Group2)

14.3.2.2.5

S3/S4/S5 entry

Below are S3/S4/S5 entry sequences. There are 2 parts to S3/S4/S5 Entry.
• S-State D3 Entry
• PG/CLK Control
• USB S3 Entry Control
14.3.2.2.5.1

S-State D3 Entry (SMU)

D3 entry sequence in S3/S4/S5 entry sequence is the same as all other D3 (Hot/Cold) entry sequences. Refer to earlier
section on D3Hot/D3Cold Entry.
14.3.2.2.5.2

PG/CLK Control in S3/S4/S5 (BIOS)

[AMD Confidential - Distribution with NDA]

56176 Rev 3.10 - Aug 18, 2020

PPR for AMD Family 17h Model 71h B0

When the OS informs the BIOS that the system will be entering S3/S4/S5 (e.g via ACPI _PTS method), BIOS performs
the following sequence:
1. Poll
USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::CURRENT_POWER_STATE_CNTR0[CURRENT_POWER_STATE]
until it is 11b (D3). This step may take up to 150ms.
a.If
USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::CURRENT_POWER_STATE_CNTR
0[CURRENT_POWER_STATE] does not go to 2'b11 after T_UsbD3Entry, move to next step.
2. Send USB_S3_ENTRY message to SMU FW.
a.USB needs T_UsbIsoOn to complete the internal S3 entry sequence.
14.3.2.2.5.3

USB S3 Entry Control(SMU)

After the D3 entry sequence, SMU FW waits for BIOS USB_S3_ENTRY message.
1. When SMU FW receives USB_S3_ENTRY message from BIOS for S3 entry, SMU FW starts below steps.
2. Program to 1'b1.
a.This informs USB controller to isolate its S5 power domain, as system will be entering low-power state.
3. Check USB_RSMU_PME_TO_ACK through USB RSMU usb_rsmu_pwrmgt_intr_1 until it is 1'b1.
a.USB needs T_UsbIsoOn to complete the internal S3 entry sequence.
14.3.2.2.6

S3 Exit (SMU Firmware and BIOS)

Below are S3 exit sequences. There are 2 parts to S3 Exit:
• PG/CLK Control
• S3 D3 Exit
After clearing USB rsmu_hard_resetb on S0 power-up, SMU FW waits for BIOS's message for the current system power
state (S3 exit).
14.3.2.2.6.1

PG/CLK Control in S3 (BIOS)

1. After BIOS USB code starts running, BIOS sends USB_CONFIG messages to pass programming information of
platform independent and dependent registers to SMU FW.
14.3.2.2.6.2

S3 D3 Exit(SMU)

D3 Exit after S3 is very similar to a non-S3 D3 Exit. Listed below are the differences:
The S3 D3 Exit sequence is triggered by BIOS, while a non-S3 D3 Exit is triggered by an nBIF interrupt generated when
the driver writes D0 to PMCSR.PowerState.
1. After SMU firmware receives USB_CONFIG messages from BIOS for Group2 and Group3 register programming
information, SMU FW saves the register information for the 2 groups.
2. When SMU firmware receives USB_S3_EXIT message from BIOS for S3 exit, SMU firmware starts below steps.
3. Program USB SMU assist Power State Control register, SMU_CTL_Power_State bits
(USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::SMU_ASSIST_POWER_STATE_CONTROL_CNTR
0[SMU_CTL_POWER_STATE]) to 2'b00.
• For S3, there is no need to wait for an OS D0 write as USB PMCSR register is already in D0 due to S0
power shut-off. In addition, the OS D0 write (D0→D0) can't trigger nBIF to generate interrupt.
4. Poll USB CURRENT_POWER_STATE bits
(USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::CURRENT_POWER_STATE_CNTR
0[CURRENT_POWER_STATE]) until the read value is 2'b00 (D0 state). The step may take T_UsbD3Exit.
5. Program USB Host Controller (Group 3) registers:
1. Platform-Independent Configuration Programming.

[AMD Confidential - Distribution with NDA]

AMD Confidential - Advance Information
56176 Rev 3.10 - Aug 18, 2020

PPR for AMD Family 17h Model 71h B0

2. Platform-Dependent Configuration Programming.
6. Below steps to work around multiple PME_STATUS clear issue.
1. Read from USB Shadowed PMCSR register, PME_Status bit ().
2. If PME_Status bit is 0, write 0 to PME_Status bit () again with other bits unaltered.
3. If PME_Status bit is 1, skip.

BIOS Menu Options and Sub-sequences

14.3.2.4.1

BIOS Menu Options

The platform configuration features described in chapter 1.2.9 can be enabled/disabled or configured through BIOS menu
options. The chapter lists the features to be covered using BIOS menu options.
14.3.2.4.1.1

SuperSpeed Link Speed Limit

The link speed limit feature is described in chapter SuperSpeed Link Speed Limit. A BIOS menu option is required to
enable/disable speed limit feature for each SuperSpeed port.
The menu option shall provide options to users to limit SuperSpeed gen2 ports to gen1 operation individually via
USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::PORT_CONTROL_CNTR0 registers.

The registers (one per controller) are USB container registers (group1). By hardware default, the speed limit is disabled
for all ports. When enable the speed limit on some of the SuperSpeed ports, a USB_CONFIG message for the group1
register setting needs to be generated.
14.3.2.4.1.2

Over-current Control

The over-current mapping is described in chapter Overcurrent Mapping. A BIOS menu option is required to enable and
reassign over-current pin for each port.
The menu option shall provide options to users, via
USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::OVERCURRENT_MAP_0_CNTR0, to:
• Enable or disable over-current for each port individually.
• Assign an OC pin to a port.
The registers (one per controller) are USB container registers (group1). By hardware default, over-current for all ports are
disabled and chapter Group 1 includes over-current assignment programming for Gonzalo reference board. When change
over-current settings for some ports, the USB_CONFIG message for the BIOS Menu Options and Sub-sequences.
14.3.2.4.2

Sub-Sequence

There are currently one fixed sub-sequences, PHY SRAM firmware loading sequence programming sequence.
14.3.2.4.2.1

USB31 PHY SRAM Firmware Loading Sub-sequence

When requested, it can be enabled through USB_CONFIG message with opcode 0xC0 and parameter 0x01. Refer to
Table 6 ~ Table 9 for USB_CONFIG message formats.
The SRAM loading sub-sequence needs to be executed every time after the PHY is reset through phy_reset.
a.Poll register, sram_init_done bit, until the read value is 1'b1.
b.SMU FW communicates with PSP FW to start PHY SRAM loading sequence.
c.On reception of SMU FW request for PHY FW loading, PSP FW retrieves PHY firmware binary code and writes the
firmware code to PHY SRAM through APB interface
• USB APB offset range for USB31 PHY SRAM is 0x0013_8000 ~ 0x0013_BFFF.
• The SRAM locations can be written only one offset at a time through APB interface with no burst.
d.Program to 1'b1.
• The step signals completion of firmware loading to PHY.
14.3.2.5

RSMU Interrupt from USB

USB has 10 RSMU power-management interrupts for use in controlling power management sequences. Currently only
intr_1 is used and needs to be enabled.

usb_rsmu_pwrmgt_intr_1 is used for acknowledgement (USB_RSMU_PME_TO_ACK) to PME_TURN_OFF (which is
from SMU through writes to register RESET_SEQ_CTRL_CNTR0). The interrupt shall be enabled.

[AMD Confidential - Distribution with NDA]

2386

AMD Confidential - Advance Information
56176 Rev 3.10 - Aug 18, 2020
14.3.2.6

PPR for AMD Family 17h Model 71h B0

Current Power Status for USB

Please note that the read value of USB Current Power State register, Current_power_state bits reflect the current power
state of USB host.
When enter into D3 cold state, don't start to remove the power until Current_power_state is read as 2'b11 (D3).
When exit from D3 state, don't start the host transactions until Current_power_state is read as 2'b00 (D0).
14.3.2.7

S-State Entry/Exit

The implementation of the host controller is compliant to the xHCI standard with regard to saving state and powering
down as well as powering up and restoring state. As such it is compatible with standard xHCI drivers. There are however
a number of implementation specific programming steps for the BIOS to indicate S-State entry and exit to the USB
controller so that it can properly support Wake/PME. Note that the steps described below are already part of the S-State
Entry and Exit sequences specified in previous sections, this section is purely informative.
• S-State Entry
• Use standard software steps to save xHC state (xHCI 1.1 Specification, Section 4.23.2)
• Enable desired wake conditions via PORTSC (WCE, WDE, WOE)
• Use standard PCI Power Management interface to enable PME and place xHC in D3.
• BIOS sends USB_S3_ENTRY message to SMU to trigger SMU sequence for USB S3 entry. SMU sequence then
writes to registers, PME_TURN_OFF field.
• This informs USB controller that system will be entering low-power state in which USB should not be
reset.
• SMU needs to wait for acknowledgment (USB_RSMU_PME_TO_ACK through USB_RSMU_pwrmgt_intr_1)
before informing BIOS that USB is ready for system S3 entry.
• After SMU FW returns for USB_S3_ENTRY message, BIOS waits T_UsbIsoOn for USB to complete the internal
S3 entry sequence.
• S-State Exit
• BIOS sends USB_S3_EXIT message to SMU to trigger SMU sequence for USB S3 exit.
• SMU then executes USB S3 Exit sequence defined in chapter S3 Exit.
• Use standard software steps to restore xHC state (xHCI 1.1 Specification, Section 4.23.2)
14.3.2.8

Platform/Customer Configuration Features

This section describes a number of common platform configuration features.The programming of these features would
generally occur during the Platform-Dependent Register Configuration of the Reset and Power State Transition
Sequences.
14.3.2.8.1

Number of Ports

This feature allows a platform to expose fewer ports to software than are physically present in the USB host controller.
This configuration is implemented via the USB2_NUM_PORTS and USB3_NUM_PORTS fields of the
PORT_CONTROL_CNTR register (USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::PORT_CONTROL_CNTR0).
Valid values of USB2_NUM_PORTS is from 1 to the actual number of USB2 ports implemented in the host controller.
Valid values of USB3_NUM_PORTS is from 1 to the actual number of USB3 ports implemented in the host controller.
xHCI HCSPARAMS1.MaxPorts = USB2_NUM_PORTS + USB3_NUM_PORTS.
14.3.2.8.2

Port Disable

This feature allows a platform to disable ports such that the ports do not report connect/disconnect events, and always
remain in the disabled state. This feature is configured via the USB2_PORT_DISABLE and USB3_PORT_DISABLE

14.3.2.8.3

Overcurrent Mapping

This feature allows a platform to map SOC overcurrent inputs to USB ports. Overcurrent mapping is configured via the
USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::OVERCURRENT_MAP_0_CNTR0 and
USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::OVERCURRENT_MAP_1_CNTR0 registers. A four-bit field is allocated for
each USB port in the SOC. For an SOC with M USB2 ports and N USB3 ports, USB2 ports are numbered 0 to M and
USB3 ports are numbered M+1 to M+N. For overcurrent mapping purposes, port numbers are not affected by any change
to USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::PORT_CONTROL_CNTR0[USB2_NUM_PORTS] or
USB31::USBCONTAINERREGCNTR0::PORT_CONTROL_CNTR0[USB3_NUM_PORTS]
PORTx_OVERCURRENT_SELECT = Fh maps no overcurrent pin to Port x, effectively disabling overcurrent detection
for Port x.
14.3.2.8.4

SuperSpeed Link Speed Limit Control

This feature allows a platform to limit a SuperSpeed Gen2 capable port to Gen1 operation. This feature is configured via
the PORT_CONTROL_CNTR register. To enable the Link Speed Limit feature on Host Controller N, Port P:
• Set PORT_CONTROL_CNTRN.USB31_PORT_FORCE_GEN1_EN[P]

USB3 Compliance Mode

The USB3 specification defines that a downstream port shall disable its transition path from Polling.LFPS to Compliance
Mode upon PowerOn Reset or Warm Reset. The method to direct a USB3 downstream port to enable the transition path
from Polling. LFPS to Compliance is defined in the xHCI specification. If the port is in the Disconnected state, a write to
PORTSC with PORTSC.PLS=10d (Compliance Mode) enables the transition to Compliance Mode.

14.3.2.12

Periodic idle interval interrupt Handling

14.3.2.12.1

Interrupt configuration

USB supports the periodic idle interval interrupt. The interrupt is one of sources of usb_rsmu_pwrmgt_intr_5 to rsmu. To
enable the periodic idle interval interrupt, FW should configure USB registers and rsmu registers firstly.
For USB registers, the configuration described in chapter 14.3.2.2.4.2 [Cold Boot, System Reset, S4/S5 Exit, Link Reset
Init (SMU)], section b of step 7 about periodic_idle_interval_threshold () and section c of step 7.
For RSMU registers, FW should configure the usb_rsmu_pwrmgt_intr_5 in a general interrupt configuration routine, it
includes to configure the interrupt type to edge type, interrupt enable, interrupt priority, etc. Since it is a standard sequence
for MP1 power management interrupt, it is not part of this document.
1/1.0/main/doc/remote_smu_mas_Pwrmgt_Security_Interrupt.doc.

[AMD Confidential - Distribution with NDA]

2389

AMD Confidential - Advance Information
56176 Rev 3.10 - Aug 18, 2020
14.3.2.12.2

PPR for AMD Family 17h Model 71h B0

Interrupt service

After received the interrupt, SMU FW should handle the following steps:
Step1: read the register bit "USB Activity INT REQ[2]" ()
a) If it is 1'b1, it means all of intervals of periodic idle is lager than periodic threshold time (=4'hf, 2ms) during the
periodic filter time (=4'h0, 4ms), USB has no periodic transfer. FW can set DF to enter a low power state: Cstates. (Please check with DF how to handle it)
b) If it is 1'b0, it means any one interval of periodic idle is less than or equal to periodic threshold time (=4'hf, 2ms)
during the periodic filter time (=4'h0, 2ms), USB has the periodic transfer, FW should disable DF to enter a low
state. (Please check with DF how to handle it)
Step2: read the register bit "USB activity intr status[2]" (), it should be 1'b1 to indicate it is periodic idle interval interrupt
status.
Step3: write 1'b1 to register bit "USB activity intr status[2]" () to clear the interrupt status.

USB0x000028 (FCHUSBDWCUSB31CNTR0::PAGESIZE)
Read-only.
Page Size Register Bit Definitions
Use this register to enable or disable the reporting of specific USB Device Notification Transaction Packets being
received.
A Notification Enable (Nx, where x = 0 to 15) flag is defined for each of the 16 possible device notification types. If a
flag is set for a specific notification type, a Device Notification Event is generated when the respective notification
packet is received. After reset, all notifications are disabled.
This register is written as a Dword. Byte writes produce undefined results.

BESL. Read-write. Reset: 0h.
Description: Best Effort Service Latency (BESL) - RW.
Default = '0'. System software sets this field to indicate to the recipient device how long the xHC will drive
resume if it (the xHC) initiates an exit from L1.
The BESL value is encoded as follows: Value Description 0h 50us. (default) 1h 125us. 2h 200us. Fh 1.175 ms.
The value of 0000b is interpreted as 50us. Each incrementing value up adds 75us. to the previous value.
For example, 0001b is 125us, 0010b is 200us and so on. Based on this rule, the maximum value resume drive
time is at encoding value 1111b which represents 1.2ms.
Note that the BESL field is used by both software and hardware controlled LPM.

For a description of this standard USB register field, see the eXtensible Host Controller Interface for Universal
Serial Bus (USB) Specification 3.1.
BESL. Read-write. Reset: 0h.
Description: Best Effort Service Latency (BESL) - RW.
Default = '0'. System software sets this field to indicate to the recipient device how long the xHC will drive
resume if it (the xHC) initiates an exit from L1.
The BESL value is encoded as follows: Value Description 0h 50us. (default) 1h 125us. 2h 200us. Fh 1.175 ms.
The value of 0000b is interpreted as 50us. Each incrementing value up adds 75us. to the previous value.
For example, 0001b is 125us, 0010b is 200us and so on. Based on this rule, the maximum value resume drive
time is at encoding value 1111b which represents 1.2ms.
Note that the BESL field is used by both software and hardware controlled LPM.

3

Refer to section 4.23.5.1.1 for more information on BESL use. Refer to Section 4.1 of the USB2 LPM spec for
more information on the use of the BESL field.

Description: Remote Wake Enable
System software sets this flag to enable or disable the device for remote wake from L1.

For a description of this standard USB register field, see the eXtensible Host Controller Interface for Universal
Serial Bus (USB) Specification 3.1.
L1S. Read-only. Reset: 0h.
Description: L1 Status (L1S) - RO. Default = 0.
This field is used by software to determine whether an L1-based suspend request (LMP transaction) was
successful, specifically:
Value Meaning 0 Invalid - This field is ignored by software.
- 1 Success - Port successfully transitioned to L1 (ACK)
- 2 Not Yet - Device is unable to enter L1 at this time (NYET)
- 3 Not Supported -Device does not support L1 transitions (STALL)
- 4 Timeout/Error -Device failed to respond to the LPM Transaction or an error occurred
- 5-7 Reserved The value of this field is only valid when the port resides in the L0 or L1 state (PLS = '0' or '2').
Refer to section 4.23.5.1.1 for more information.

Description: L1DSLOT

7:4

For a description of this standard USB register field, see the eXtensible Host Controller Interface for Universal
Serial Bus (USB) Specification 3.1.
BESL. Read-write. Reset: 0h.
Description: Best Effort Service Latency (BESL) - RW.
Default = '0'. System software sets this field to indicate to the recipient device how long the xHC will drive
resume if it (the xHC) initiates an exit from L1.
The BESL value is encoded as follows: Value Description 0h 50us. (default) 1h 125us. 2h 200us. Fh 1.175 ms.
The value of 0000b is interpreted as 50us. Each incrementing value up adds 75us. to the previous value.
For example, 0001b is 125us, 0010b is 200us and so on. Based on this rule, the maximum value resume drive
time is at encoding value 1111b which represents 1.2ms.
Note that the BESL field is used by both software and hardware controlled LPM.

3

Refer to section 4.23.5.1.1 for more information on BESL use. Refer to Section 4.1 of the USB2 LPM spec for
more information on the use of the BESL field.
RWE. Read-write. Reset: 0.
Description: Remote Wake Enable
System software sets this flag to enable or disable the device for remote wake from L1.

2:0

For a description of this standard USB register field, see the eXtensible Host Controller Interface for Universal
Serial Bus (USB) Specification 3.1.
L1S. Read-only. Reset: 0h.
Description: L1 Status (L1S) - RO. Default = 0.
This field is used by software to determine whether an L1-based suspend request (LMP transaction) was
successful, specifically:
Value Meaning 0 Invalid - This field is ignored by software.
- 1 Success - Port successfully transitioned to L1 (ACK)
- 2 Not Yet - Device is unable to enter L1 at this time (NYET)
- 3 Not Supported -Device does not support L1 transitions (STALL)
- 4 Timeout/Error -Device failed to respond to the LPM Transaction or an error occurred
- 5-7 Reserved The value of this field is only valid when the port resides in the L0 or L1 state (PLS = '0' or '2').
Refer to section 4.23.5.1.1 for more information.

PPR for AMD Family 17h Model 71h B0

Reset: 0000_0FA0h.
Interrupter Moderation Register
The software may use this register to pace (or even out) the delivery of interrupts to the host CPU.
This register provides a deterministic inter-interrupt delay between interrupts asserted by the xHC, regardless of USB
traffic conditions.
To independently validate configuration settings, software may use the following algorithm to convert the inter-interrupt
Interval value to the common 'interrupts/sec' performance metric.

USB0x0005C4 (FCHUSBDWCUSB31CNTR0::IMAN_REGS7_IMOD)
Reset: 0000_0FA0h.
Interrupter Moderation Register
The software may use this register to pace (or even out) the delivery of interrupts to the host CPU.
This register provides a deterministic inter-interrupt delay between interrupts asserted by the xHC, regardless of USB
traffic conditions.
To independently validate configuration settings, software may use the following algorithm to convert the inter-interrupt
Interval value to the common 'interrupts/sec' performance metric.
_instUSB0_aliasHOST; USB0x0005C4; USB0={NBIFEPFNCFG::BASE_ADDR_2_nbio0_instNBIF1_dev0_func3_aliasHOST[BASE_ADDR] ,
NBIFEPFNCFG::BASE_ADDR_1_nbio0_instNBIF1_dev0_func3_aliasHOST[BASE_ADDR]}

Bits Description
31:16 IMODC. Read-write,Volatile. Reset: 0000h.
Description: Interrupt Moderation Counter (IMODC)
- RW.
Default = undefined. Down counter.
Loaded with the IMODI value whenever IP is cleared to '0', counts down to '0', and stops. The associated interrupt
is signaled whenever this counter is '0', the Event Ring is not empty, the IE and IP flags = '1', and EHB = '0'. This
counter may be directly written by software at any time to alter the interrupt rate.
15:0 IMODI. Read-write. Reset: 0FA0h.
Description: Interrupt Moderation Interval (IMODI) - RW.
Default = '4000' (~1ms). Minimum inter-interrupt interval. The interval is specified in 250ns increments.
A value of '0' disables interrupt throttling logic and interrupts is generated immediately if IP = '0', EHB = '0', and
the Event Ring is not empty.

USB0x00C10C (FCHUSBDWCUSB31CNTR0::GRXTHRCFG)
Global Rx Threshold Control Register
There is an issue when ACK TP with NumP=0 followed by ACK TP with NumP=1 without ERDY TP sent by the device
controller during a Burst BULK OUT transfer. This may cause third-party 3.0 host controllers to keep waiting for the
ERDY TP.
The USB 3.0 Specification states that "When an endpoint is not in a flow control condition, it shall not send an ERDY
TP unless the endpoint is a Bulk endpoint that supports streams." In this case, after the device sent the ACK TP
(nump=1), the endpoint was not in the flow control, so it did not send an ERDY.
The device would have sent ERDY if the next OUT packet was not received. When the next OUT packet was received,
at that time there was enough buffer space to accept it, so the device accepted the packet by informing host that it is no
longer in the flow control. The Host should wait for the responses for all the OUT packets to return and then decide if the
endpoint is still in flow control or not.
The USB 3.1 Specification supersedes all the USB 3.0 specification. The errata states that "If the host continues, or
resumes, transactions to an endpoint, the endpoint shall re-evaluate its flow control state and respond appropriately."
However, there are no ECNs on the USB 3.0 for this issue.
To work around this issue, the Global Rx Threshold mode must be disable by setting GRXTHRCFG.UsbRxPktCntSel =
'0'. Instead, software can program the DCFG.NUMP mode (where fixed NUMP is transmitted always) instead of the RX
threshold based nump mode to prevent the device from sending ACK TP with NumP=0. The NUMP in the ACK TP is
the minimum value of (DCFG.NUMP, bMaxBurstSize) for each endpoint.
IN Transfer Concurrency: When threshold mode is enabled, the Host controller disables IN transfer concurrency. The
Host controller will execute IN transfers to one endpoint at a time in order to adhere to the maximum throughput limit
specified by the threshold settings.

NBIFEPFNCFG::BASE_ADDR_1_nbio0_instNBIF1_dev0_func3_aliasHOST[BASE_ADDR]}

Description: USB HS High Bandwidth Periodic Receive Packet Threshold Enable - Host Mode Only
This field enables/disables the USB reception multi-packet thresholding:
- 0: USB HS High Bandwidth Periodic Receive multi-packet thresholding is disabled; The controller can start

- 1: USB HS High Bandwidth Periodic Receive multi-packet thresholding is enabled; the controller can only start
reception on the USB when the RXFIFO has space for at least UsbRxThrNumPkt_HS_Prd amount of packets.
This mode is valid in host mode for high speed high bandwidth periodic endpoints.

Note: The intent of using this bit is only when the system bus is slow and not able to cater to the data rate of
High-Bandwidth endpoint (3076 bytes/uframe). If the system bus is slow, and if all the transactions of a HighBandwidth endpoint could not be executed successfully, it would likely cause a compliance test failure (section
5.4.x of xHCI Compliance Test Specification). This issue is seen only with older PCI based USB-IF compliance
devices.

31:19 PWRDNSCALE. Read-write. Reset: 000Ch.
Description: Power Down Scale
The USB31 core_suspend_clk input replaces core_pipe_pclk as a clock source to a small part of the USB31
controller that operates when the ESS PHY is in its lowest power (P3) state, and therefore does not provide a
clock.
The Power Down Scale field specifies how many core_suspend_clk periods fit into a 16 kHz clock period. When
performing the division, round up the remainder.
For example, when using an 8-bit/16-bit/32-bit PHY and 25-MHz Suspend clock,
Power Down Scale = 25000 kHz/16 kHz = 13'd1563 (rounder up)
Note:
- Minimum Suspend clock frequency is 32 kHz
- Maximum Suspend clock frequency is 125 MHz
The LTSSM uses Suspend clock for 12-ms and 100-ms timers during suspend mode. According to the USB 3.1
specification, the accuracy on these timers is 0% to +50%.
- 12 ms + 0~+50% accuracy = 18 ms (Range is 12 ms - 18 ms)
- 100 ms + 0~+50% accuracy = 150 ms (Range is 100 ms - 150 ms).
The suspend clock accuracy requirement is:
- (12,000/62.5) * (GCTL[31:19]) * actual Suspend clock period must be between 12,000 and 18,000
- (100,0000/62.5) * (GCTL[31:19]) * actual Suspend clock period must be between 100,000 and 150,000
For example, if core_suspend_clk frequency varies from 7.5 MHz to 10.5MHz, then the value needs to
programmed is:
Power Down Scale = 10500/16 = 657 (rounded up; and fastest frequency used).
Same requirement is applicable to suspend_clk

If this bit is,

- 1: the link waits for 8us of LFPS before it detects a valid U2 exit.
This bit is added to improve interoperability with a third party host controller. This host controller in U2 state
while performing receiver detection generates an LFPS glitch of about 4us duration. This causes the device to exit
from U2 state because the LFPS filter value is 248ns. With the new functionality enabled, the device can stay in
U2 while ignoring this glitch from the host controller.

29 FILTER_SE0_FSLS_EOP. Read-write. Reset: 1.
Description: FILTER_SE0_FSLS_EOP
- 0: Single sampling (utmi/ulpi clock) of linestate is checked for SE0 detection.
- 1: Feature enabled; Two samplings of linestate are checked for SE0 detection
This bit is applicable for FS/LS operation. If this feature is enabled, SE0 on the linestate is validated for two
consecutive utmi/ulpi clock edges for EOP detection. This feature is applicable only in FS in device mode and
FS/LS mode of operation in host mode.
- Device mode (FS): If GUCTL1.FILTER_SE0_FSLS_EOP is set, then for device LPM handshake, the controller
ignores single SE0 glitch on the linestate during transmit. Only two or more SE0 is considered as a valid EOP on
FS port.
- Host mode (FS/LS): If GUCTL1.FILTER_SE0_FSLS_EOP is set, then the controller ignores single SE0 glitch
on the linestate during transmit. Only two or more SE0 is considered as a valid EOP on FS/LS port.
Enable this feature if linestate has SE0 glitches during transmission. This bit is quasi-static, that is, it must not be
changed during operation.
28 TX_IPGAP_LINECHECK_DIS. Read-write. Reset: 0.
Description: TX_IPGAP_LINECHECK_DIS
- 0: The linestate transitioning from J to idle for HS mode treated as end of current packet.
- 1: Feature enabled; For detecting the HS end of packet, a fixed delay is used instead of linestate transition.
This bit is applicable for HS operation of U2MAC. If this feature is enabled, then the 2.0 MAC operating in HS
ignores the UTMI/ULPI linestate during transmission of a token (during token-to-token and token-to-data
IPGAP). When enabled, the controller implements a fixed 40-bit TxEndDelay after the packet is given on UTMI
and ignores the linestate during this time. This feature is applicable only in HS mode of operation.
- Device mode: If GUCTL1.TX_IPGAP_LINECHECK_DIS is set, then for device LPM handshake, the
controller ignores the linestate after TX and waits for a fixed number of clocks (40 bit times equivalent) after
transmitting ACK on utmi.
- Host mode: If GUCTL1.TX_IPGAP_LINECHECK_DIS is set, then the ipgap (between token to token/data) is
added by 40 bit times of TXENDDELAY, and linestate is ignored during this 40 bit times delay.
Enable this bit if linestate does not reflect the expected line state (J) during transmission. This bit is quasi-static,
that is, it must not be changed during operation.

Description: Sparse Control Transaction Enable
Some devices are slow in responding to Control transfers. Scheduling multiple transactions in one

16

If this bit is set to 1'b1, the host controller schedules each phase of a Control transfer in different

ResBwHSEPS. Read-write. Reset: 1.
Description: Reserving 85% Bandwidth for HS Periodic EPs (ResBwHSEPS)
- 1'b0: HC reserves 80% of the bandwidth for periodic EPs.
- 1'b1: HC relaxes the bandwidth to 85% to accommodate two high-speed high-bandwidth ISOC EPs.
USB 2.0 required 80% bandwidth allocated for ISOC traffic. If two high-bandwidth ISOC devices (HD
Webcams) are connected and each device requires 1024-bytes X 3 packets per micro-frame, then the bandwidth
required is around 82%. If this bit is set, then it is possible to connect two Webcams of 1024bytes X 3 paylod per
micro-frame each. Otherwise, you may have to reduce the resolution of the Webcams.
Reserved.
USBHstInImmRetryEn. Read-write. Reset: 1.
Description: Host IN Immediate Retry (USBHstInImmRetryEn)
When set, this field enables the Immediate Retry feature. For IN transfers (non-isochronous) that encounter data
packets with CRC errors or internal overrun scenarios, the immediate retry feature causes the Host controller to
reply to the device with a non-terminating retry ACK (that is, an ACK transaction packet with Retry = 1 and
NumP != 0).

13

12

If the Immediate Retry feature is disabled, the controller will respond with a terminating retry ACK (that is, an
ACK transaction packet with Retry = 1 and NumP = 0).
- 1'b0: Immediate Retry Disabled
- 1'b1: Immediate Retry Enabled
EnOverlapChk. Read-write. Reset: 0.
Description: Enable Check for LFPS Overlap During Remote Ux Exit:
If this bit is set to,
- 1'b1: The Enhanced SuperSpeed link when exiting U1/U2/U3 waits for either the remote link LFPS or TS1/TS2
training symbols before it confirms that the LFPS handshake is complete. This is done to handle the case where
the LFPS glitch causes the link to start exiting from the low power state. Looking for the LFPS overlap makes
sure that the link partner also sees the LFPS.
- 1'b0: When the link exit U1/U2/U3 because of a remote exit, it does not look for an LFPS overlap.
ExtCapSupptEN. Read-write. Reset: 0.
Description: External Extended Capability Support Enable (ExtCapSuptEN)
When set, this field enables extended capabilities to be implemented outside the controller.
When the ExtCapSupEN is set and the Debug Capability is enabled, the Next Capability pointer in "Debug
Capability" returns 16.
